rules.statement: A Run that has reached a terminal status never transitions again. succeeded, failed, cancelled and timed_out have no successors, and a command asking a Run to leave one of them is refused as an illegal transition.
examples: A cancel arriving after the Run already succeeded is refused, not applied.
A late provider callback reporting failure on a Run that already timed out is refused, so the recorded outcome does not change after the fact.
A Run in evaluating may still move to succeeded, failed, cancelled or timed_out, because evaluating is not terminal.

approvals.scope: The finality of a terminal Run status, as the transition table, the terminality test and the transition guard establish it

rules.statement: Interactive Skill creation does not import the Contexts it collaborates with, and none of them imports it. Everything it needs from the reference, admission and trial Contexts arrives as a narrow interface injected by a composition root, so the creation loop can be replaced or removed without any other Context changing.
examples: Enqueueing a creation job goes through an interface the wiring package supplies, not through the queue Context's own Service.
A Context that wants to know what a creation session produced reads the Skill Version the session created, not the session.
Credit and identity are reached the same way every other Context reaches them, because neither is part of the creation loop being kept replaceable.

approvals.scope: the inversion rule and the two replaced policies
